title: Backlog workspace-default-by-platform: one workspace default helper, gate staleness for run lead files, portable run lead files

tasks.grade_reason: a new shared helper in shell and Python, a new suite and its registration
tasks.objective: Backlog topic workspace-default-by-platform item 1, part 1. When RPG_FACTORY_WORKSPACE is unset, scripts and suites default the workspace to the WSL drive form of Workspaces/UnityIndie, which fails on Git Bash for Windows. tests/routing.test.sh already has default_workspace() (an explicit non-empty RPG_FACTORY_WORKSPACE wins; the Git Bash drive form on MINGW, MSYS and Cygwin by uname -s; the WSL form elsewhere). Make it the one shared helper: (a) a new sourceable scripts/lib/workspace.sh defining rpgf_default_workspace with exactly that behaviour (uname looked up at call time so a test can stub it; no side effects when sourced); (b) default_workspace(env=None, nt=None) in scripts/lib/workspace.py with the same rule for Python (explicit env value wins; otherwise the WSL form passed through native_path, so Windows Python gets the drive-letter form); keep workspace.py stdlib-only and cheap to import. Switch tests/routing.test.sh to source the shell helper (keep its export and its stubbed-uname self-tests working) and switch the workspace defaults inside tests/run-all.sh to the helper. New suite tests/workspace-default.test.sh covering both helpers with a stubbed platform (Git Bash, MSYS, Cygwin, Linux, explicit value wins, empty value falls back), registered in tests/run-all.sh like the other suites, listed in tests/README.md and scripts/README.md (one line each). Changelog fragment changelog.d/workspace-default.md (### Fixed). Do not touch other callers (task workspace-callers).
acceptance: one shell and one Python helper give the same default on every platform; an explicit value wins
routing.test.sh and run-all.sh use the helper; the new suite is registered and passes
the file guard and hooks that import workspace.py stay stdlib-only and fast

an exported RPG_FACTORY_WORKSPACE still wins in every caller

tasks.grade_reason: gate logic: a wrong exemption lets untested code through READY_FOR_PR
tasks.objective: Backlog topic workspace-default-by-platform items 2 and 3, in scripts/factory-pipeline.py. (1) gate marks the integration QA STALE whenever the integration HEAD differs from the QA SHA (the 'QA is STALE (ran on' blocker), so a commit that only changes run lead files (run_lead_files(): the plan file, its report.md, the backlog.md beside it) forces a 15-20 minute rerun of the workspace QA. Treat the QA as current when the QA SHA is an ancestor of HEAD and every file changed between them is a run lead file; any other changed file, a non-ancestor QA SHA or a failing git command keeps the STALE blocker (fail safe). (2) In plan ci-backlog-followups the run lead committed a plan and report containing machine-specific path text; only CI's parallel-policy portable-plans case caught it, after the PR was open. Make gate also check the run lead files present on the integration branch with the same machine-path rule the portable-plans case of tests/parallel-policy.test.sh uses, and report a blocker naming the file. Move that regex into one place that both the test and factory-pipeline.py use (for example scripts/lib/plan_paths.py) so they cannot drift; the parallel-policy case keeps its mutations and passes. Tests in tests/pipeline.test.sh: a report-only commit after QA keeps READY_FOR_PR; a code commit after QA is STALE; a run lead file with a machine path blocks the gate. Document both in docs/pipeline-cli.md ('gate'), and rewrap the lines of docs/pipeline-cli.md that are longer than 120 columns (backlog item 3). Changelog fragment changelog.d/gate-lead-files.md (### Changed).
acceptance: a commit of run lead files only after integration QA does not make it STALE; any other file does
gate blocks a run lead file with machine-specific path text, using the same rule as the portable-plans case
docs/pipeline-cli.md has no line over 120 columns
